edition/year: Wiley, first published 2012 (commonly cited 2013); print ISBN 9781119994336, online ISBN 9781118443118
scope summary: Comprehensive SHM textbook casting the problem as machine learning/statistical pattern recognition. Chapters cover operational evaluation, sensing/data acquisition, case studies, probability/statistics, damage-sensitive features, nonlinear-response features, supervised/unsupervised learning, data normalization, SHM axioms and damage prognosis.
overlap: Substantial overlap with existing D2 Los Alamos review, B1 SAMCO, E2 system-identification material and newer open review literature. The book adds coherent pedagogy, worked examples and deep treatment of feature engineering, novelty detection and normalization rather than unique architecture requirements.
recommendation: MEDIUM-LOW — seek institutional e-book/WorldCat loan or buy used; buy new only for the analytics work package or team training, not as an architecture prerequisite.
rationale: High technical quality and durable reference value, especially for environmental/operational variability and novelty detection, but the current task is system architecture and governance. Wiley's official page and Google Books expose a detailed TOC sufficient to confirm fit before purchase.
